name: Ruby2Shell
tile_line: Researchers: default Rails, classic Sinatra reach it.
tldr: A one-byte memory bug in how Ruby changes the case of text in some single-byte encodings like ISO-8859-1 may let an attacker with no login run code. Exploit shown, not public. Researchers say default Rails and classic Sinatra apps reach it: upgrade Ruby.
summary: The fix is a Ruby upgrade, which also fixes six related regex and string bugs. Veria Labs plans to publish its proof of concept on 25 Nov 2026.

affected.label: Ruby older than the fix
affected.text: Affected: 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0–3.4.12 and 4.0.0–4.0.9. Ruby 3.2 and older are end of life and won't get a fix. Check the Ruby your app actually runs (its container image or `.ruby-version`), not just the system one. Distros may patch without changing the version; on 20 Nov Ubuntu (priority Medium) and Debian were still evaluating.

affected.label: Web input gets case-changed
affected.text: Veria Labs says default Rails and classic-style Sinatra apps reach the bug with no login, but hasn't said through which code path. Other frameworks and plain Rack aren't exposed by default, unless your code calls `upcase`, `swapcase`, `downcase(:fold)` or `casecmp?` on ISO-8859 or Windows-125x text; UTF-8 isn't affected by this bug. A separate case-conversion bug fixed in the same releases (GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px) needs text whose case-changed result is over 4 GiB, and Ruby doesn't limit it to these encodings. Sources disagree on reach: Ruby rates it Critical, the CVE record scores it 7.4 (local), and Sekurak thinks a crash is likelier than code execution. Run the check in your app's folder.

do.label: Upgrade Ruby
do.text: To 3.3.14, 3.4.13 or 4.0.10. Then restart app servers and rebuild container images. Updating Rails or other gems doesn't help: the fix is in Ruby itself.

do.label: On Ruby 3.2 or older? Move up
do.text: These are end of life and won't be fixed. Move to a supported series.

do.label: Update self-hosted apps
do.text: Some bundle their own Ruby, which a system upgrade doesn't touch. Fixed: GitLab 19.6.1, 19.5.8 and 19.4.10 (20 Nov), Chatwoot 4.20.1 (20 Nov), Mastodon 4.7.6, 4.6.12, 4.5.22 and 4.4.29, OpenProject 17.9.8 and 17.8.3, and the Discourse base image 2.0.20261119-0203. GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22.6 (22 Nov) updated Ruby "to fix several announced vulnerabilities" without naming this one; Veria's list, last updated 21 Nov before that release, shows it as vulnerable. For GitLab, check its bundled Ruby with the command below.

do.label: Can't upgrade yet?
do.text: Ruby gives no workaround. For self-hosted apps, Aikido suggests keeping them reachable only over VPN or an IP allowlist until the vendor ships a fix.

do.label: Patch before the exploit is out
do.text: Veria Labs said it would publish its proof of concept on 25 Nov 2026, or later if major vendors hadn't shipped a fix by then. On 26 Nov 2026 its write-up still said that, and it hadn't published one.
